findings.message: 1000 RCU provisioned against a 0.0 consumed average (no measured reads); 1000 WCU provisioned against a 0.0 consumed average (no measured writes) - about $569.40/month of unused capacity
table is encrypted with the AWS-owned key, which has no key policy, no grants and no CloudTrail trail of its own - a customer-managed-key requirement cannot be met
GSI by-status consumed 0.000 capacity units on average over 14d - it is paid for on every write and read by nobody
GSI by-customer projects ALL, so every write to the 8.0 GiB base table is replicated in full into the index (6.0 GiB); switch to KEYS_ONLY or INCLUDE with the attributes the query actually reads
provisioned mode with no Application Auto Scaling target for ReadCapacityUnits, WriteCapacityUnits - capacity only ever changes when a human notices
deletion protection is off on a table holding 2,412,880 items
point-in-time recovery is not enabled, so there is no restore window - this cannot be switched on retroactively
TTL is disabled on a table of 8.0 GiB taking 30.0 WCU of sustained writes; growth is inferred, pass --compare-json <older dump> for a measured delta
500 RCU provisioned against a 40.0 consumed average (12.5x) - about $43.65/month of unused capacity
on-demand traffic is flat (cv 0.04) and costs about $98.55/month; 125 RCU / 50 WCU provisioned with 20% headroom would cost about $35.59/month

pricing_note: Prices are us-east-1 DynamoDB Standard list prices (provisioned $0.00013/RCU-hour, $0.00065/WCU-hour; on-demand $0.125/M read request units, $0.625/M write request units). Other regions cost more - override with --price-rcu-hour, --price-wcu-hour, --price-read-request, --price-write-request.
